f.title: Submit a proposed REMS as part of the application when FDA determines a REMS is necessary
f.statement: If FDA determines that a risk evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS) is necessary to ensure that the benefits of the drug outweigh its risks and informs the person submitting the application, that person shall submit a proposed REMS to FDA as part of the application.
f.applicability: Applications for initial approval of a drug for which FDA has determined a REMS is necessary

f.statement: A REMS communication plan may include sending letters to health care providers; disseminating information about the REMS elements to encourage implementation by providers or explain safety protocols such as periodic laboratory monitoring; disseminating information through professional societies about serious risks and protocols to assure safe use; or disseminating information about drug formulations or properties, their limitations or patient care implications, and how they may relate to serious adverse drug events.

f.title: Make the drug available in unit-dose or set-duration packaging, or with safe disposal packaging, when the REMS requires it
f.statement: Where FDA requires it in the REMS for a drug with a serious risk of an adverse drug experience from overdose or abuse, the drug must be made available for dispensing to certain patients in unit dose packaging, packaging that provides a set duration or another packaging system that FDA determines may mitigate the risk, or be dispensed to certain patients with safe disposal packaging or a safe disposal system where FDA determines it may mitigate the risk and is sufficiently available.
f.applicability: Drugs with a serious risk of an adverse drug experience from overdose or abuse (subsection (b)(1)(B) or (C))

f.title: Make the elements to assure safe use commensurate with the specific serious risk in the labeling
f.statement: Elements to assure safe use (ETASU) shall be commensurate with the specific serious risk listed in the labeling of the drug.

f.title: Design ETASU so they are not unduly burdensome on patient access and fit established distribution and dispensing systems
f.statement: ETASU shall not be unduly burdensome on patient access to the drug, considering in particular patients with serious or life-threatening conditions, patients who have difficulty accessing health care (such as in rural or medically underserved areas) and patients with functional limitations; and, to the extent practicable and to minimise the burden on the health care delivery system, shall conform with ETASU for other drugs with similar serious risks and be designed to be compatible with established distribution, procurement and dispensing systems.
f.applicability: Drugs whose REMS includes elements to assure safe use

rows.review_note: Review: checked against the source; quote, statement, level and classification confirmed. Double-check: quote verbatim, statement within the quote, level follows the modal verb.

f.title: Include one or more goals in the ETASU; prescriber or dispenser certification may be required, with access for frontier-area providers
f.statement: ETASU shall include one or more goals to mitigate a specific serious risk listed in the labeling. To mitigate the risk they may require that prescribers have particular training or experience or are specially certified (with training or certification available to any willing frontier-area provider through a widely available method, such as an online course or by mail, at reasonable cost), and that pharmacies, practitioners or health care settings that dispense the drug are specially certified (with certification available to any willing frontier-area provider).
f.applicability: Drugs whose REMS includes elements to assure safe use

f.title: Withdraw the Board review request or end administrative appeals once the review is scheduled and noticed
f.statement: When a Drug Safety Oversight Board review has been scheduled and notice of it has been posted, the responsible person shall either withdraw the request for review or terminate the use of administrative appeals.
f.applicability: Covered applications (NDA under section 505(b) and BLA under PHS Act section 351, per 355(p)(1)(A)); not ANDAs, which are subject only to the listed-drug elements in subsection (i)

f.title: Reach agreement with FDA on the REMS before the decision, ending the dispute resolution process
f.statement: At any time before a decision and order is issued, FDA and the responsible person may reach agreement on the REMS through further discussion or administrative appeals, which terminates the dispute resolution process; FDA then issues an action letter or order describing the strategy.

f.title: As an ANDA, follow the listed drug's Medication Guide/PPI, packaging or disposal and ETASU, via a shared system or a comparable aspect
f.statement: A drug that is the subject of an ANDA is subject only to the following elements of the REMS required for the applicable listed drug: a Medication Guide or patient package insert, a packaging or disposal requirement, and ETASU, if required for the listed drug. For ETASU the ANDA may use a single, shared system with the listed drug or a different, comparable aspect of the ETASU.
f.applicability: ANDAs under section 505(j) whose listed drug has a REMS

rows.quote:
A drug that is the subject of an abbreviated new drug application under section 355(j) of this title is subject to only the following elements of the risk evaluation and mitigation strategy required under subsection (a) for the applicable listed drug:
(A) A Medication Guide or patient package insert, if required under subsection (e) for the applicable listed drug.
(B) A packaging or disposal requirement, if required under subsection (e)(4) for the applicable listed drug.
(C)(i) Elements to assure safe use, if required under subsection (f) for the listed drug, which, subject to clause (ii), for a drug that is the subject of an application under section 355(j) of this title may use—
(I) a single, shared system with the listed drug under subsection (f); or
(II) a different, comparable aspect of the elements to assure safe use under subsection (f).

f.title: Use a single, shared system with the listed drug for ETASU when FDA requires it
f.statement: FDA may require an ANDA drug and its listed drug to use a single, shared system for ETASU if it determines that no different, comparable aspect of the ETASU could satisfy subsection (f); the ANDA and listed drug holders must then use the shared system.

f.title: Use an FDA-approved different, comparable aspect of ETASU for other ANDAs or 505(b) applications referencing the same listed drug
f.statement: Where FDA approves a different, comparable aspect of ETASU for an ANDA drug, FDA may require that it can be used for any other drug that is the subject of an ANDA or a 505(b) application referencing the same listed drug.

f.title: Providing samples to an eligible product developer does not violate the REMS
f.statement: Providing samples of a covered product to an eligible product developer (as defined in 21 U.S.C. 355-2(a)) is not considered a violation of the requirements of any REMS in place for the drug.

f.title: Make a different, comparable aspect of ETASU achieve the same level of safety as the listed drug's strategy
f.statement: A different, comparable aspect of the ETASU is a REMS for an ANDA drug that uses different methods or operational means than the strategy for the applicable listed drug, or another ANDA with the same listed drug, but achieves the same level of safety as that strategy.
f.applicability: ANDAs using a separate REMS (different, comparable aspect of ETASU)

rows.quote: When used in this section, the term "different, comparable aspect of the elements to assure safe use" means a risk evaluation and mitigation strategy for a drug that is the subject of an application under section 355(j) of this title that uses different methods or operational means than the strategy required under subsection (a) for the applicable listed drug, or other application under section 355(j) of this title with the same such listed drug, but achieves the same level of safety as such strategy.
